mainTopic: Examples of real disputes for each phrase of the זקן ממרא פסוק: דין, דם, דין לדין, and נגע
overview: The גמרא is going word by word through the פסוק about the זקן ממרא, 'כי יפלא ממך דבר למשפט, בין דם לדם, בין דין לדין, בין נגע לנגע'. For each phrase it gives a real dispute that could come before the בית דין הגדול. For 'למשפט', which means a דין, the example is the law of בתו מאנוסתו, learned through two גזירה שוה derivations, 'הנה' and 'זמה'. 'בין דם לדם' covers three kinds of blood. For נדה, the dispute is עקביא בן מהללאל against the חכמים about green blood. For לידה, it is רב against לוי on whether there is one source or two. For זיבה, it is רבי אליעזר against רבי יהושע about a woman who had relief from labor before giving birth. 'בין דין לדין' covers money cases (can two judges rule), capital cases (does 'a life for a life' mean money), and lashes (three judges or twenty-three). 'בין נגע לנגע' covers נגעים of a person, of houses, and of garments, with a dispute for each. The dispute about garments, between רבי יונתן בן אבטולמוס and the רבנן, continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The example of 'דין' (for 'למשפט'): a man's daughter from a woman he raped
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the example of 'דין', the word it used to explain 'למשפט' in the פסוק: the law of בתו מאנוסתו, which is learned through a גזירה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another example is the law of a man's daughter born from a woman he raped.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is giving its example for the word 'למשפט' in the פסוק, which it explained as 'דין'. The example is the law of בתו מאנוסתו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה clearly forbids a man's wife's daughter. A daughter from a woman he raped is not his wife's daughter, so that פסוק does not cover her. Her איסור and her punishment have to be learned another way, which the next step will show.

keyTerms.meaning: The law of, the ruling about
His daughter
A woman he raped (and did not marry)

phrases.english: The law of his daughter from the woman he raped.
phrases.notes: This is the example for 'למשפט – זה הדין', a law we only know by learning it out with a גזירה שוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the example for 'למשפט – זה הדין', continuing the גמרא's word-by-word explanation of the פסוק from the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The law of בתו מאנוסתו is the example of a 'דין', a law derived by גזירה שוה, which could be brought before the בית דין הגדול.

steps.title: Where the law of the rape-born daughter comes from
steps.stepSummary: רבא reports in the name of רב יצחק בר אבודימי that this law comes from two גזירה שוה derivations: 'הנה–הנה' and 'זמה–זמה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבא said: רב יצחק בר אבודימי told me, it is learned from the word 'הנה' and the word 'הנה'. It is learned from the word 'זמה' and the word 'זמה'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the source for the law of בתו מאנוסתו. It is not written outright, so it is learned through two word-comparisons (גזירה שוה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first comparison, 'הנה–הנה', links the פסוק about a granddaughter to the פסוק about a wife's daughter. This teaches that one's own daughter is forbidden too. The second comparison, 'זמה–זמה', links to the פסוק that gives the punishment of שריפה, so this איסור also carries death by burning. Because the law is learned through דרשה rather than stated outright, it is the kind of issue a בית דין could disagree about.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes (is learned) from, the formula for a גזירה שוה
'They' or 'theirs', a word found in two פסוקים about forbidden relatives
'Lewdness', a word used in the עריות פסוקים, including the one that gives the punishment of burning
Learning a law by comparing the same word used in two places

steps.confusionAlert: There are two separate גזירה שוה derivations here, and each one does a different job. 'הנה' teaches that the daughter is forbidden, and 'זמה' teaches that the punishment is burning.

phrases.english: As רבא said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לִי רַב יִצְחָק בַּר אֲבוּדִימִי,
phrases.english: רב יצחק בר אבודימי said to me,
it is learned from 'הנה' and 'הנה',
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:10 and ויקרא 18:17. Both פסוקים use the word 'הנה'.

phrases.english: it is learned from 'זמה' and 'זמה'.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:17 and ויקרא 20:14. The second פסוק is where the punishment of burning is written.

steps.triggerLanguage: דאמר רבא אמר לי רב יצחק בר אבודימי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the law named in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That a man's daughter from a woman he raped is forbidden and punished by burning
steps.raayaSupportSource: Two גזירה שוה derivations, 'הנה–הנה' and 'זמה–זמה', from רבא in the name of רב יצחק בר אבודימי
steps.whatToRemember: The example of a 'דין' (for the word 'למשפט') is בתו מאנוסתו, a capital law that comes from two גזירה שוה derivations: 'הנה' teaches the איסור and 'זמה' teaches burning.

steps.title: 'Between blood and blood' means three kinds of blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the phrase 'בין דם לדם' and explains that it refers to דם נדה, דם לידה and דם זיבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Between blood and blood': this means between the blood of נדה, the blood of לידה (childbirth), and the blood of זיבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section, explaining the next phrase in the פסוק. 'בין דם לדם' refers to the three types of a woman's blood, and the גמרא is setting up examples for each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each type of blood has its own rules about טומאה and about when marital relations are forbidden. The גמרא will now give an example of a real dispute for each type, starting with דם נדה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Between blood and blood', a phrase from the פסוק in דברים 17:8
Menstrual blood
Blood after childbirth
Blood of זיבה, a discharge outside the normal cycle

phrases.english: 'Between blood and blood' –
between the blood of נדה,
the blood of childbirth, the blood of זיבה.

steps.triggerLanguage: בין דם לדם בין דם נדה דם לידה דם זיבה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves 'למשפט – זה הדין' and starts explaining the next phrase of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'בין דם לדם' covers disputes about דם נדה, דם לידה and דם זיבה.

steps.title: The example for menstrual blood: the dispute about green blood
steps.stepSummary: For דם נדה, the example is the מחלוקת between עקביא בן מהללאל and the חכמים, as the משנה teaches: about green blood, עקביא says it is טמא and the חכמים say it is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: For דם נדה, the example is the dispute between עקביא בן מהללאל and the חכמים. As we learned in a משנה: about green blood, עקביא בן מהללאל declares it impure, and the חכמים declare it pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first example under 'בין דם לדם'. A real dispute about דם נדה is whether green blood counts as נדה blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to עקביא בן מהללאל, green blood makes a woman a נדה, so relations with her would be an איסור כרת. According to the חכמים, it does not make her a נדה, so there is no איסור. This is exactly the kind of serious disagreement that could go up to the בית דין הגדול.

keyTerms.meaning: A dispute
As we learned in a משנה
Green blood
Declares impure
Declare pure

phrases.english: The blood of נדה –
it is about the dispute of עקביא בן מהללאל and the רבנן,
as we learned: green blood –
עקביא בן מהללאל declares it impure,
and the חכמים declare it pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: דם נדה בפלוגתא עקביא בן מהללאל ורבנן דתנן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first specific example, for דם נדה, of the three types of blood listed in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That there is a real dispute about דם נדה which fits 'בין דם לדם'
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about green blood (נדה 19a): עקביא בן מהללאל says טמא, the חכמים say טהור

steps.title: Example for דם לידה: רב says the blood after birth comes from one source
steps.stepSummary: For דם לידה, the גמרא points to the מחלוקת between רב and לוי. רב holds that it is all one source, and the תורה alone decides when it is טמא and when it is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Blood of childbirth refers to the dispute between רב and לוי. As it was stated, רב said: It is one source. The תורה made it impure, and the תורה made it pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its second example of 'בין דם לדם', this time for blood after childbirth, and begins with רב's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After a birth there is a set time of טומאה, followed by days when blood is טהור. רב says the blood comes from one source the whole time. Nothing physical changes; the תורה simply declares the same flow טמא at first and טהור afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood a woman sees after giving birth
A dispute or argument between Sages
As it was stated (introduces a statement of אמוראים)
A source or spring (here, the source of the blood)

phrases.english: Blood of childbirth refers to the dispute of רב and לוי,
as it was stated: רב said:
It is one source;
the Torah made it impure, and the Torah made it pure.
phrases.notes: It's the same flow: טמא in the first days after birth, טהור in the days after. Only the Torah's timing changes it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the דם נדה example (step 4) to the second kind of blood listed in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That 'בין דם לדם' includes a dispute about דם לידה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The מחלוקת of רב and לוי, starting with רב's view of one source

steps.title: לוי says the blood after birth comes from two separate sources
steps.stepSummary: לוי disagrees with רב. He says there are two sources: when the impure one closes, the pure one opens, and when the pure one closes, the impure one opens.
steps.simpleTranslation: And לוי said: They are two sources. When the impure one is closed, the pure one is opened. When the pure one is closed, the impure one is opened.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side of the דם לידה dispute, לוי's view, which completes the example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For לוי, טמא and טהור blood come from two different places, so the status depends on which source is actually flowing. If bleeding continues without a break past the set time, the two views can reach different results about whether she is still a נדה. That decides whether relations with her carry כרת, which is why this counts as a case of 'בין דם לדם'.

keyTerms.meaning: Is closed or sealed
Is opened
Ritually impure / ritually pure

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב and לוי argue about how many days are טמא or טהור. Both agree on the תורה's timeline. They argue about what the blood is, one source or two, and that only matters in cases like a continuous flow.

phrases.english: And לוי said: They are two sources;
when the impure one is closed, the pure one is opened;
when the pure one is closed, the impure one is opened.
phrases.notes: This is the switch back at the end of the pure days, when blood becomes טמא again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רב, completing the דם לידה example.
steps.raayaObject: That 'בין דם לדם' includes a dispute about דם לידה
steps.raayaSupportSource: לוי's view that there are two separate sources

steps.title: Example for דם זיבה: רבי אליעזר's view in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: For דם זיבה, the גמרא points to the מחלוקת of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע in a משנה. A woman bled with labor pains for three days during the eleven days. If she then had relief for a full 24 hours before giving birth, רבי אליעזר says she gives birth as a זבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Blood of זיבה refers to the dispute of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע, as we learned in a משנה: If a woman had hard labor for three days within the eleven days, and she had relief for a full 24 hours and then gave birth, she is one who gives birth as a זבה. These are the words of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its third example, for דם זיבה, by quoting a משנה. It starts with רבי אליעזר's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood that comes from labor is not זיבה. But if the labor stopped for 24 hours before the birth, the earlier three days of blood were not birth-related, so they make her a זבה. רבי אליעזר says any 24 hours of relief is enough to give her the status of a יולדת בזוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood seen outside the normal נדה time, which can make a woman a זבה
As we learned in a משנה
She had hard labor (with bleeding)
She had relief, a break from the labor
A full 24-hour period, starting from any time
A woman who gives birth while in the status of a זבה

phrases.english: Blood of זיבה refers to the dispute
of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.
As we learned in a משנה: If she had hard labor for three days
within the eleven days,
phrases.notes: These are the days between נדה periods. Bleeding then for three days in a row makes a woman a זבה.

phrases.english: if she had relief for a full 24 hours and then gave birth,

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זוֹ יוֹלֶדֶת בְּזוֹב, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר.
phrases.english: she is one who gives birth as a זבה; these are the words of רבי אליעזר.

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּם זִיבָה – בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the דם לידה example to the third kind of blood listed in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That 'בין דם לדם' includes a dispute about דם זיבה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in מסכת נדה, starting with רבי אליעזר's view

steps.title: רבי יהושע requires a night and a day of relief from pain
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע says the 24 hours must be a night followed by its day, like Friday night and the day of שבת. The relief means relief from pain, even if the blood kept flowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע says: A night and a day, like the night of שבת and its day, when she had relief from the pain and not from the blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה with רבי יהושע's view, which completes the דם זיבה example and the whole list for 'בין דם לדם'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע defines the break differently. It must be a night followed by a day, not just any 24 hours, and it means relief from the pain, not from the blood. Since the two disagree about when she is a יולדת בזוב, they also disagree about whether she must count seven clean days as a זבה. If she has not done so, relations with her could still carry כרת. That makes this a כרת question of 'בין דם לדם'.

keyTerms.meaning: A night followed by a day
Like Friday night and the day of שבת after it
Pain (here, labor pain)

steps.whatToRemember: 'בין דם לדם' covers three kinds of blood, each with a dispute that can decide כרת. דם נדה: עקביא and the חכמים about green blood. דם לידה: רב (one source) against לוי (two sources). דם זיבה: רבי אליעזר (any 24 hours) against רבי יהושע (a night and a day of relief from pain).

phrases.english: And רבי יהושע says: A night and a day,
like the night of Shabbos and its day,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁשָּׁפְתָה מִן הַצַּעַר וְלֹא מִן הַדָּם.
phrases.english: when she had relief from the pain and not from the blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יהושע's opposing view in the same משנה, completing the דם זיבה example.
steps.raayaObject: That 'בין דם לדם' includes a dispute about דם זיבה
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע's view in the משנה in מסכת נדה

steps.title: Defining 'between judgment and judgment'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that בין דין לדין refers to three kinds of court cases: דיני ממונות, דיני נפשות, and דיני מכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Between judgment and judgment' means between money cases, capital cases, and cases of lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next phrase of the פסוק and explains what kinds of 'judgments' it means. This sets up the next steps, which give an example for each kind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as בין דם לדם was split into three kinds of blood, בין דין לדין is split into three kinds of court cases. Each one will be matched with a known מחלוקת where an elder could argue with the court.

keyTerms.meaning: Money cases, where the court decides who must pay whom
Capital cases, about life and death
Cases where the punishment is lashes

phrases.english: 'Between judgment and judgment':
phrases.notes: דברים 17:8, the next phrase in the same פסוק, right after בין דם לדם.

phrases.english: between money cases,
capital cases, and cases of lashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the three kinds of blood (Steps 4-8), the גמרא moves on to the next phrase in the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בין דין לדין covers money cases, capital cases, and cases of lashes.

steps.title: Money cases: שמואל on a court of two judges
steps.stepSummary: For דיני ממונות, the example is the מחלוקת of שמואל and רבי אבהו. שמואל says a ruling by two judges counts, but they are called a brazen court.
steps.simpleTranslation: Money cases: this is the argument between שמואל and רבי אבהו. שמואל says that if two judges decided a case, their ruling counts, but they are called a brazen court.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the example for money cases: the argument of שמואל and רבי אבהו. This step brings שמואל's side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A money case normally needs three judges. שמואל says that if only two judged, the ruling still stands. They did something improper, so they are called a בית דין חצוף.

keyTerms.meaning: A dispute or argument between חכמים
A brazen court: judges who acted with too few members

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל does not say two judges are allowed to judge. He says that after the fact the ruling counts, but they acted wrongly, which is why they get the name 'brazen'.

phrases.aramaic: דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת – בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דִּשְׁמוּאֵל וְרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ,
phrases.english: Money cases: this is in the dispute of שמואל and רבי אבהו,
as שמואל says:
Two who judged, their judgment is a valid judgment,
except that they are called a brazen court.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת – בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דִּשְׁמוּאֵל וְרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first of the three examples listed in Step 9.
steps.raayaObject: What kind of money-case argument could make an elder a זקן ממרא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The opinion of שמואל in his dispute with רבי אבהו about a court of two.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: a ruling by two judges does not count
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו says that everyone agrees a ruling by two judges is not valid at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אבהו says: According to everyone, their ruling is not a valid ruling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the other side of the money-case argument. רבי אבהו says a two-judge ruling does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said the ruling stands after the fact. רבי אבהו says it does not stand at all, and he claims that everyone agrees with this. So an elder and the court could disagree on whether such a ruling counts.

keyTerms.meaning: According to everyone; all opinions agree

phrases.english: And רבי אבהו says:
According to everyone, their judgment is not a valid judgment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the money-case example by giving the opposing view to שמואל.
steps.raayaObject: The money-case dispute that an elder could argue about.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The opinion of רבי אבהו against שמואל.

steps.title: Capital cases: רבי says 'a life for a life' means money
steps.stepSummary: For דיני נפשות, the example is the מחלוקת of רבי and the רבנן. רבי says the פסוק 'you shall give a life for a life' means paying money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Capital cases: this is the argument of רבי and the רבנן. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי says, 'You shall give a life for a life' means money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the example for capital cases. It quotes a ברייתא where רבי reads 'a life for a life' as a money payment, not a death penalty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether this case is a capital case at all. רבי says the person pays money. The רבנן's view is not quoted here, but since they disagree, they must read the פסוק as an actual life.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
A life for a life
Money

phrases.english: Capital cases:
this is in the dispute of רבי and the רבנן.
As it is taught: רבי says,
'And you shall give a life for a life' means money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second of the three examples from Step 9, for capital cases.
steps.raayaObject: What kind of capital-case argument could make an elder a זקן ממרא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא with רבי's reading of נפש תחת נפש.

steps.title: How רבי learns that it means money
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether the פסוק might mean an actual life. It answers that the word 'giving' appears in two nearby פסוקים, and just as one means money, so does the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say it means money, or maybe it means an actual life? 'Giving' is said above, and 'giving' is said below. Just as there it means money, here too it means money.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tests רבי's reading by asking whether the פסוק could mean an actual life. Then it proves the money reading from a word that repeats in the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same verb, 'give', is used in both פסוקים about this case. In the other פסוק the giving is clearly a money payment set by the judges. So the ברייתא reads 'give a life for a life' as money too.

keyTerms.meaning: An actual life, meaning the death penalty
Giving; the verb used in both פסוקים
Just as there, so too here; comparing two places with the same word

phrases.english: Do you say it means money,
or perhaps it means only an actual life?
'Giving' is said above,
phrases.notes: The 'giving' above is ונתן בפללים (שמות 21:22), clearly money set by judges. The other is our פסוק, ונתתה נפש (שמות 21:23).

phrases.english: and 'giving' is said below.

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְהַלָּן מָמוֹן, אַף כָּאן מָמוֹן.
phrases.english: Just as there it means money, so too here it means money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר מָמוֹן, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא נֶפֶשׁ מַמָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, showing the source for רבי's reading in Step 12.
steps.raayaObject: רבי's claim that נפש תחת נפש means money.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The repeated word נתינה in שמות 21:22 and 21:23.

steps.title: Cases of lashes: the רבנן say three judges
steps.stepSummary: For דיני מכות, the example is the מחלוקת of רבי ישמעאל and the רבנן. The משנה says lashes are judged by three.
steps.simpleTranslation: Cases of lashes: this is the argument of רבי ישמעאל and the רבנן, as the משנה teaches: Lashes are judged by three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the third example, for cases of lashes. It brings the first opinion in a משנה: three judges are enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the question is how many judges are needed to give lashes. The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה says a court of three is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
Lashes

phrases.english: Cases of lashes:
this is in the dispute of רבי ישמעאל and the רבנן,
as we learned: Lashes are judged by three.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּינֵי מַכּוֹת – בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל וְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the third and last example from Step 9, for cases of lashes.
steps.raayaObject: What kind of lashes argument could make an elder a זקן ממרא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה that says lashes need three judges.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: lashes need twenty-three judges
steps.stepSummary: In the name of רבי ישמעאל they said that lashes need a court of twenty-three.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the name of רבי ישמעאל they said: By twenty-three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the other side of the lashes argument. רבי ישמעאל says lashes need a court of twenty-three, the size used for capital cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן said three judges are enough for lashes. רבי ישמעאל treats lashes more seriously and requires twenty-three. With this, all three kinds of 'judgment' have a matching example.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of
Twenty-three, the size of a small סנהדרין

steps.whatToRemember: בין דין לדין means three kinds of cases, each with its own example. Money cases: can two judges rule (שמואל vs. רבי אבהו)? Capital cases: is 'a life for a life' money (רבי vs. רבנן)? Lashes: three judges or twenty-three (רבנן vs. רבי ישמעאל)?

phrases.english: In the name of רבי ישמעאל they said:
By twenty-three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the lashes example by giving רבי ישמעאל's view against the רבנן in Step 14.
steps.raayaObject: The lashes dispute that an elder could argue about.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי ישמעאל's opinion in the first משנה of סנהדרין.

steps.title: Defining 'between mark and mark' as three kinds of נגעים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the phrase 'בין נגע לנגע' refers to the three types of נגעים: of a person, of houses, and of garments.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Between mark and mark' means between the marks of a person, the marks of houses, and the marks of garments.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next phrase in the פסוק and explains what it covers. This sets up the examples that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as the גמרא explained the earlier categories, it now explains 'בין נגע לנגע'. The word 'נגע' covers three separate areas of הלכה, and each one has its own rules. The next steps will show a real מחלוקת in these areas.

keyTerms.meaning: A צרעת mark that can make something טמא
צרעת marks on a person's skin
צרעת marks on the walls of a house
צרעת marks on clothing

phrases.english: "Between mark and mark"
phrases.notes: דברים 17:8, the next phrase in the same פסוק.

phrases.english: means between marks of a person,
marks of houses, and marks of garments.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the three examples for בין דין לדין (steps 10-15), the גמרא moves on to the next phrase in the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'בין נגע לנגע' covers the three areas of נגעי אדם, נגעי בתים, and נגעי בגדים.

steps.title: Marks of a person: the doubtful case of בהרת and white hair
steps.stepSummary: For נגעי אדם, the example is the מחלוקת between רבי יהושע and the רבנן about a case where it is unclear whether the בהרת or the white hair came first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Marks of a person are in the dispute of רבי יהושע and the רבנן, as we learned: If the בהרת came before the white hair, he is טמא. If the white hair came before the בהרת, he is טהור. If it is unclear, he is טמא. רבי יהושע says: It is 'כהה'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a real מחלוקת in the area of נגעי אדם by quoting a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule depends on the order: a בהרת first and then white hair makes him טמא, but white hair first does not. When the order is unknown, the רבנן say טמא. רבי יהושע answers with one unclear word, 'כהה', which the גמרא will explain next.

keyTerms.meaning: A bright white skin spot, one type of צרעת mark
White hair growing in the spot, a sign of טומאה
A doubt, when we do not know the facts
Dim or faded

phrases.english: Marks of a person
are in the dispute of Rabbi Yehoshua and the Rabbis.
As we learned in a משנה:

phrases.aramaic: אִם בַּהֶרֶת קָדַם לַשֵּׂעָר הַלָּבָן – טָמֵא,
phrases.english: If the bright spot came before the white hair, he is impure;

phrases.aramaic: אִם שֵׂעָר לָבָן קָדַם לַבַּהֶרֶת – טָהוֹר,
phrases.english: if the white hair came before the bright spot, he is pure;
if it is unclear, he is impure.
Rabbi Yehoshua says: It is dim.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִגְעֵי אָדָם בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ וְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first concrete example for the category defined in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: That there is a real מחלוקת in the area of נגעי אדם.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה about the doubtful order of בהרת and white hair.

steps.title: What does 'כהה' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יהושע meant by the word 'כהה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'dim' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what רבי יהושע meant, because one word alone does not tell us his ruling. This sets up רבא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To know whether there is a real מחלוקת, we have to know רבי יהושע's actual ruling. 'כהה' does not clearly say טמא or טהור, so the גמרא asks.

keyTerms.meaning: What? (asking for the meaning)

phrases.english: What is the meaning of "dim"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of רבי יהושע's word in the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What ruling רבי יהושע gives in the doubtful case.

steps.title: רבא: 'כהה' means the person is טהור
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that רבי יהושע's 'כהה' means טהור, like a mark that has faded.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: 'Dim' means pure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question and explains that רבי יהושע rules the person טהור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So in the doubtful case the רבנן say טמא and רבי יהושע says טהור. This makes it a clear מחלוקת, which is exactly the kind of case the משנה is talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: A major אמורא who explains the word
Pure, not טמא

steps.whatToRemember: In a doubt about the order of בהרת and white hair, the רבנן say טמא and רבי יהושע says טהור.

phrases.english: Rava said:
"Dim" means pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'כהה' means טהור, so רבי יהושע disagrees with the רבנן in the doubtful case.

steps.title: Marks of houses: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון requires a corner
steps.stepSummary: For נגעי בתים, the example is the מחלוקת between רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון and the רבנן. He says a house is only טמא if the mark covers two stones on two walls in a corner.
steps.simpleTranslation: Marks of houses are in the dispute of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון and the רבנן, as we learned: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says, a house is never טמא unless the mark is seen the size of two beans, on two stones, on two walls in a corner. Its length is two beans and its width is one bean.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a real מחלוקת in the area of נגעי בתים by quoting another משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון adds a strict condition: the mark must sit in a corner, spreading over two stones on two different walls. The רבנן do not require this. So a mark on one flat wall is a real point of disagreement.

keyTerms.meaning: A type of bean, used as a size measure
A wall
A corner where two walls meet
Length and width

phrases.english: Marks of houses

phrases.aramaic: בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וְרַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: are in the dispute of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon and the Rabbis.

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר,
phrases.english: As we learned: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says,
a house is never impure
until the mark is seen the size of two beans
on two stones,
on two walls, in a corner.
Its length is like two beans, and its width is like one bean.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִגְעֵי בָתִּים בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the example for נגעי אדם, gives the example for the second category, נגעי בתים.
steps.raayaObject: That there is a real מחלוקת in the area of נגעי בתים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה quoting רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's corner requirement.

steps.title: Why does רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון require a corner?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון gets his corner requirement from. This sets up the answer from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His condition is very specific, so the גמרא wants to know what in the תורה points to a corner. The answer will come from the wording of a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason? (asking for the source)

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן?
phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the view quoted in step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק behind the requirement that the mark be in a corner.

steps.title: One 'wall' that is like 'walls' is a corner
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says both 'wall' and 'walls'. The only single wall that counts as many walls is a corner.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written 'wall' and it is written 'walls'. Which wall is like walls? You must say: this is a corner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by pointing to two different words in the פסוק about נגעי בתים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses the singular 'קיר' and the plural 'קירות'. To fit both, the mark must be in one spot that is still on more than one wall. That is a corner, where two walls meet.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written (in the פסוק)
Wall / walls
You must say (the only possible answer is)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון learns from 'קיר' and 'קירות' in the same פסוק that a house is only טמא from a mark in a corner.

phrases.english: It is written "wall" and it is written "walls."
Which is a wall that is like walls?
You must say: this is a corner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The singular 'קיר' and plural 'קירות' in one פסוק point to a corner, a single spot on more than one wall.

steps.title: The example for marks on garments: רבי יונתן בן אבטולמוס and the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: For נגעי בגדים, the example of a dispute is the מחלוקת between רבי יונתן בן אבטולמוס and the רבנן. The גמרא begins quoting the ברייתא where he asks 'from where do we know...'
steps.simpleTranslation: Marks on garments: this is the dispute between רבי יונתן בן אבטולמוס and the רבנן. As it is taught in a ברייתא: רבי יונתן בן אבטולמוס says, 'From where do we know...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the third example in its list, this time for marks on clothing, and names the people who argue about it. It is setting up the next move by starting to quote the ברייתא. The question itself finishes in the text that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as step 20. First it names a real מחלוקת, and then it shows the source for it. So far we only know who argues: one תנא against the רבנן. What they argue about is about to be shown in the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Marks of צרעת that appear on clothing
A dispute or argument between Sages
The Sages, meaning the majority opinion
As it is taught in a ברייתא
From where do we know? This asks for the source of a law

steps.confusionAlert: The word מנין is not the end of the sentence. It opens a question, and the ברייתא continues right after this.

phrases.english: Marks on garments:

phrases.aramaic: בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹנָתָן בֶּן אַבְטוּלְמוֹס וְרַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: this is the dispute between Rabbi Yonatan ben Avtolemos and the Rabbis.
As it is taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן בֶּן אַבְטוּלְמוֹס אוֹמֵר, מִנַּיִן
phrases.english: Rabbi Yonatan ben Avtolemos says: From where do we know...

steps.triggerLanguage: נִגְעֵי בְגָדִים בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹנָתָן בֶּן אַבְטוּלְמוֹס וְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the source for the נגעי בתים example (steps 20-22), the גמרא moves to the next category on its list, נגעי בגדים.
steps.raayaObject: Shows what the משנה means by a dispute about נגעים, using the case of garments.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא with the מחלוקת between רבי יונתן בן אבטולמוס and the רבנן.
